typeHeader: TYPE - VIII: BASED ON POLICE AND THIEF
questionText: A thief noticed a policeman at a distance of $600\text{ metres}$. The thief started running and the policeman chased him. The thief and policeman are running at speeds of $12\text{ km/h}$ and $15\text{ km/h}$, respectively. Find the time (in minutes) required for the policeman to catch the thief.
solution:
$\text{Relative speed} = 15 - 12 = 3\text{ km/h} = 3 \times \frac{5}{18} = \frac{5}{6}\text{ m/s}$.

$\text{Time required} = \frac{\text{Distance}}{\text{Relative speed}} = \frac{600}{\frac{5}{6}} = 720\text{ seconds} = \frac{720}{60} = 12\text{ minutes}$.

typeHeader: TYPE - VIII: BASED ON POLICE AND THIEF
questionText: A thief is noticed by a policeman from a distance of $200\text{ m}$. The thief starts running and the policeman chases him. The thief and the policeman run at the rate of $10\text{ km/h}$ and $11\text{ km/h}$, respectively. What is the distance (in metres) between them after $9\text{ minutes}$?
solution:
$\text{Relative speed} = 11 - 10 = 1\text{ km/h} = \frac{1000\text{ m}}{60\text{ min}} = \frac{50}{3}\text{ m/min}$.

Distance gained by policeman in $9\text{ minutes} = \frac{50}{3} \times 9 = 150\text{ m}$.

$\text{Distance between them} = 200 - 150 = 50\text{ m}$.

typeHeader: TYPE - VIII: BASED ON POLICE AND THIEF
questionText: A thief pursued by a policeman was $150\text{ m}$ ahead at the start. If the ratio of the speed of the policeman to that of the thief was $5 : 4$, then how far (distance in metres) could the thief go before he is caught by the policeman?
solution:
Since time is constant, $\frac{D_{\text{police}}}{D_{\text{thief}}} = \frac{S_{\text{police}}}{S_{\text{thief}}} = \frac{5}{4}$.

Difference in distance $= 5 - 4 = 1\text{ unit} = 150\text{ m}$.

$\text{Distance run by thief} = 4 \times 150 = 600\text{ m}$.

typeHeader: TYPE - VIII: BASED ON POLICE AND THIEF
questionText: A thief is spotted by a policeman from a distance of $200\text{ metres}$. When the policeman starts the chase, the thief also starts running. Difference $= 10 - 9 = 1\text{ unit} = 200\text{ m} = 0.2\text{ km}$.

$\text{Distance run by thief} = 9 \times 0.2 = 1.8\text{ km}$.

typeHeader: TYPE - VIII: BASED ON POLICE AND THIEF
questionText: A thief is spotted by a policeman from a distance of $195\text{ metres}$. When the policeman starts the chase, the thief also starts running. $\text{Distance run by thief} = 22 \times 39 = 858\text{ m}$.

typeHeader: TYPE - VIII: BASED ON POLICE AND THIEF
questionText: A thief is noticed by a policeman from a distance of $92\text{ m}$. The thief starts running and the policeman chases him. The thief and the policeman run at the speed of $90\text{ km/h}$ and $104.4\text{ km/h}$, respectively. In how much time will the policeman catch the thief?

typeHeader: TYPE - VIII: BASED ON POLICE AND THIEF

questionText: A policeman is chasing a thief at a speed of $82\text{ km/h}$. The thief is $1300\text{ m}$ away and is running at a speed of $64\text{ km/h}$. In how much time will the policeman catch the thief if both are riding on bikes?

typeHeader: TYPE - VIII: BASED ON POLICE AND THIEF
questionText: A policeman noticed a thief at some distance. The policeman started running to catch the thief and the thief also started running at the same time. solution:
$\text{Relative speed} = 12 - 10 = 2\text{ km/h}$.

$\text{Initial distance} = \text{Relative speed} \times \text{Time} = 2\text{ km/h} \times \frac{30}{60}\text{ h} = 1\text{ km} = 1000\text{ metres}$.

typeHeader: TYPE - VIII: BASED ON POLICE AND THIEF
questionText: A thief takes off on his bike at a certain speed, after seeing a police car at a distance of $250\text{ m}$. The police car starts chasing the thief and catches him. If the thief runs $1.5\text{ km}$ before being caught and the speed of the police car is $70\text{ km/h}$, then what is the speed of thief's bike (in km/h)?
solution:
Distance run by thief $= 1.5\text{ km} = 1500\text{ m}$.

Distance run by police car $= 1500 + 250 = 1750\text{ m} = 1.75\text{ km}$.

Since time is constant, $\frac{S_{\text{thief}}}{S_{\text{police}}} = \frac{D_{\text{thief}}}{D_{\text{police}}} \implies \frac{S_{\text{thief}}}{70} = \frac{1500}{1750} = \frac{6}{7}$.

$S_{\text{thief}} = 70 \times \frac{6}{7} = 60\text{ km/h}$.

typeHeader: TYPE - VIII: BASED ON POLICE AND THIEF
questionText: The speed of a thief is $\frac{4}{5}$ times of the speed of a policeman. The thief covers a distance of $6\text{ km}$ before he was caught by the policeman in $30\text{ minutes}$. Initially, what was the distance between the policeman and the thief in km?
solution:
Speed of thief $= \frac{6\text{ km}}{30/60\text{ h}} = 12\text{ km/h}$.

Since $S_{\text{thief}} = \frac{4}{5} S_{\text{police}}$, $S_{\text{police}} = 12 \times \frac{5}{4} = 15\text{ km/h}$.

Distance covered by policeman in $30\text{ min} = 15 \times 0.5 = 7.5\text{ km}$.

$\text{Initial distance} = 7.5 - 6 = 1.5\text{ km}$.

typeHeader: TYPE - VIII: BASED ON POLICE AND THIEF
questionText: A policeman received information that a thief is at a distance of $1.5\text{ km}$ from him. The thief starts moving by car and the policeman chases him by car. typeHeader: TYPE - VIII: BASED ON POLICE AND THIEF
questionText: A thief steals an item and escapes, running at $13.5\text{ km/h}$. A policeman arrives at the spot of the crime after $8\text{ minutes}$ and immediately starts chasing the thief. $28\text{ minutes}$ after the policeman started to chase the thief, there is still a gap of $540\text{ m}$ between the two. At what distance from the spot of the crime would the policeman catch up with the thief, and what is the speed (in km/h) at which the policeman ran?
solution:
Thief runs for $8 + 28 = 36\text{ minutes} = 0.6\text{ hours}$.

Distance covered by thief $= 13.5 \times 0.6 = 8.1\text{ km} = 8100\text{ m}$.

Gap remaining $= 540\text{ m}$. Distance covered by policeman in $28\text{ min} = 8100 - 540 = 7560\text{ m} = 7.56\text{ km}$.

$\text{Speed of policeman} = \frac{7.56}{28/60} = 7.56 \times \frac{15}{7} = 16.2\text{ km/h}$.

Relative speed $= 16.2 - 13.5 = 2.7\text{ km/h}$. Initial gap after $8\text{ min} = 13.5 \times \frac{8}{60} = 1.8\text{ km}$.

Time to catch $= \frac{1.8}{2.7} = \frac{2}{3}\text{ hours}$. Distance from spot of crime $= 16.2 \times \frac{2}{3} = 10.8\text{ km}$.

questionText: A policeman spots a thief at a distance of $360\text{ m}$. Both the policeman and the thief simultaneously start running, with the former chasing the latter. typeHeader: TYPE - VIII: BASED ON POLICE AND THIEF
questionText: A thief steals an item and escapes, running at a speed of $15\text{ km/h}$. solution:
Thief runs for $4 + 16 = 20\text{ minutes} = \frac{1}{3}\text{ hour}$.

Distance run by thief in $20\text{ min} = 15 \times \frac{1}{3} = 5\text{ km} = 5000\text{ m}$.

Distance covered by policeman in $16\text{ min} = 5000 - 200 = 4800\text{ m} = 4.8\text{ km}$.

$\text{Speed of policeman} = \frac{4.8}{16/60} = 4.8 \times \frac{15}{4} = 18\text{ km/h}$.

Initial gap after $4\text{ min} = 15 \times \frac{4}{60} = 1\text{ km}$.

Relative speed $= 18 - 15 = 3\text{ km/h}$. Time to catch $= \frac{1}{3}\text{ hour}$.

$\text{Distance from spot of crime} = 18 \times \frac{1}{3} = 6\text{ km}$.

$\text{Time taken by B} = \frac{90}{10} = 9\text{ hours}$.

typeHeader: TYPE - VIII: BASED ON POLICE AND THIEF
questionText: A thief steals a van at 3:00 a.m. and drives it at a speed of $57\text{ km/h}$. The theft is discovered at 4:00 a.m. and the owner starts the chase with another van at a speed of $76\text{ km/h}$. At what time will he catch the thief?
solution:
Distance covered by thief in $1\text{ hour}$ (3:00 to 4:00 a.m.) $= 57\text{ km}$.

$\text{Relative speed} = 76 - 57 = 19\text{ km/h}$.

$\text{Time to catch} = \frac{57}{19} = 3\text{ hours}$.

$\text{Catching time} = \text{4:00 a.m.} + 3\text{ hours} = \text{7:00 a.m.}$

typeHeader: TYPE - VIII: BASED ON POLICE AND THIEF
questionText: A thief steals an item and escapes, running at $20\text{ km/h}$. A policeman arrives at the spot of the crime after $6\text{ minutes}$ and immediately starts chasing the thief. $24\text{ minutes}$ after the policeman started to chase the thief, there is still a gap of $400\text{ m}$ between the two. At what distance from the spot of crime would the policeman catch up with the thief, and what is the speed at which the policeman ran?
solution:
Thief runs for $6 + 24 = 30\text{ minutes} = 0.5\text{ hours}$.

Distance covered by thief $= 20 \times 0.5 = 10\text{ km} = 10000\text{ m}$.

Distance covered by policeman in $24\text{ min} = 10000 - 400 = 9600\text{ m} = 9.6\text{ km}$.

$\text{Speed of policeman} = \frac{9.6}{24/60} = \frac{9.6}{0.4} = 24\text{ km/h}$.

Initial gap after $6\text{ min} = 20 \times \frac{6}{60} = 2\text{ km}$.

Relative speed $= 24 - 20 = 4\text{ km/h}$. Time to catch $= \frac{2}{4} = 0.5\text{ hours}$.

$\text{Catch distance} = 24 \times 0.5 = 12\text{ km}$.

typeHeader: TYPE - VIII: BASED ON POLICE AND THIEF
questionText: A thief stole jewellery from a shop at 8:15 p.m. and left on a bike at a speed of $60\text{ km/h}$. The police were informed at 8:30 p.m. If the police want to arrest the thief at 9:00 p.m., what should be the minimum speed of the police jeep?
solution:
Thief travels from 8:15 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. ($45\text{ minutes} = \frac{3}{4}\text{ hour}$).

Distance covered by thief $= 60 \times \frac{3}{4} = 45\text{ km}$.

Police travels from 8:30 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. ($30\text{ minutes} = \frac{1}{2}\text{ hour}$).

$\text{Required speed of police jeep} = \frac{45}{\frac{1}{2}} = 90\text{ km/h}$.

typeHeader: TYPE - VIII: BASED ON POLICE AND THIEF
questionText: A thief escapes from a police station at 8.00 a.m. on a cycle at a speed of $50\text{ km/h}$. A policeman starts chasing the thief on a motorbike at 9 : 30 a.m. at the speed of $65\text{ km/h}$. At what distance from the police station will the policeman catch up with the thief?
solution:
Distance covered by thief from 8:00 to 9:30 a.m. ($1.5\text{ hours}$) $= 50 \times 1.5 = 75\text{ km}$.

$\text{Relative speed} = 65 - 50 = 15\text{ km/h}$.

$\text{Time to catch} = \frac{75}{15} = 5\text{ hours}$.

$\text{Distance from police station} = 65 \times 5 = 325\text{ km}$.

typeHeader: TYPE - VIII: BASED ON POLICE AND THIEF
questionText: A starts walking at $4\text{ km/hr}$ and after $4\text{ hours}$, B starts cycling from the same point as that of A, in the same direction at $10\text{ km/hr}$. After how much distance from the starting point will B catch up with A (Correct to two decimal places)?
solution:
Distance covered by A in $4\text{ hours} = 4 \times 4 = 16\text{ km}$.

$\text{Relative speed} = 10 - 4 = 6\text{ km/hr}$.

$\text{Time to catch} = \frac{16}{6} = \frac{8}{3}\text{ hours}$.

$\text{Distance covered by B} = 10 \times \frac{8}{3} = \frac{80}{3} \approx 26.67\text{ km}$.

typeHeader: TYPE - VIII: BASED ON POLICE AND THIEF
questionText:
Vivek starts moving at the speed of $70\text{ km/hr}$ at 8:00 a.m. Neeraj starts moving in the same direction after $4\text{ hours}$ of Vivek at the speed of $120\text{ km/hr}$. Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?
I. Neeraj and Vivek meet each other at 5:36 p.m.
II. Total distance covered by both Neeraj and Vivek till 4 p.m. is 1080 km.
solution:
Vivek's head start in $4\text{ hours} = 70 \times 4 = 280\text{ km}$. Neeraj starts at 12:00 noon.

Relative speed $= 120 - 70 = 50\text{ km/hr}$.

Time to meet $= \frac{280}{50} = 5.6\text{ hours} = 5\text{ hours } 36\text{ minutes}$.
Meeting time $= \text{12:00 noon} + 5\text{ h } 36\text{ m} = \text{5:36 p.m.}$ (Statement I is correct).

Till 4:00 p.m.: Vivek travels $8\text{ hours} \implies 8 \times 70 = 560\text{ km}$.
Neeraj travels $4\text{ hours} \implies 4 \times 120 = 480\text{ km}$.
Total distance $= 560 + 480 = 1040\text{ km} \ne 1080\text{ km}$ (Statement II is incorrect).

Hence, Only I is correct.

typeHeader: TYPE - VIII: BASED ON POLICE AND THIEF
questionText: A robber steals a bag from a man at 5 p.m. and starts running at $10\text{ km/h}$. A policeman is informed about the robbery at 5:12 p.m. and he chases him on a cycle at $15\text{ km/h}$. At what time is the robber caught by the policeman?
solution:
Distance covered by robber in $12\text{ minutes} = 10 \times \frac{12}{60} = 2\text{ km}$.

$\text{Relative speed} = 15 - 10 = 5\text{ km/h}$.

$\text{Time taken to catch} = \frac{2}{5}\text{ hours} = 24\text{ minutes}$.

$\text{Catching time} = \text{5:12 p.m.} + 24\text{ minutes} = \text{5:36 p.m.}$

typeHeader: TYPE - VIII: BASED ON POLICE AND THIEF
questionText: A police station, a bank and a safe house for the thief are in a straight line with a bank in between. The distance between the police station and the safe house is four times the distance between the bank and the safe house. After looting the bank at 9 : 15 A.M, the thief runs away. A policeman gets the information instantly and chases him at the speed of $16\text{ km/h}$. The policeman catches the thief at the gate of the safe house in fifteen minutes. What is the distance between the bank and the police station?
solution:
Distance covered by policeman from police station to safe house in $15\text{ minutes} (\frac{1}{4}\text{ hr}) = 16 \times \frac{1}{4} = 4\text{ km}$.

Given $\text{Distance}(\text{Police station to Safe house}) = 4 \times \text{Distance}(\text{Bank to Safe house})$.

$\text{Distance}(\text{Bank to Safe house}) = \frac{4}{4} = 1\text{ km}$.

Since bank is in between: $\text{Distance}(\text{Bank to Police station}) = 4 - 1 = 3\text{ km}$.

typeHeader: TYPE - VIII: BASED ON POLICE AND THIEF
questionText: A policeman follows a thief who is $600\text{ m}$ ahead of the policeman. If the policeman and the thief run at speeds of $10\text{ km/h}$ and $8\text{ km/h}$, respectively, in how much time (in minutes), will the policeman catch the thief?
solution:
$\text{Relative speed} = 10 - 8 = 2\text{ km/h} = \frac{2000\text{ m}}{60\text{ min}} = \frac{100}{3}\text{ m/min}$.

$\text{Time to catch} = \frac{600}{\frac{100}{3}} = 18\text{ minutes}$.

questionText: Places A and B are $144\text{ km}$ apart. Two cars start simultaneously, one form A and the other from B. If they move in the same direction, they meet after $12\text{ hours}$, but if they move towards each other they meet after $\frac{9}{8}\text{ hours}$. The speed (in km/h) of the car moving at a faster speed, is:
solution:
Let speeds of the cars be $x$ and $y$ ($x > y$).

Moving in same direction: $x - y = \frac{144}{12} = 12\text{ km/h}$.

Moving towards each other: $x + y = \frac{144}{\frac{9}{8}} = \frac{144 \times 8}{9} = 128\text{ km/h}$.

Adding equations: $2x = 140 \implies x = 70\text{ km/h}$.

questionText: Two places A and B are $60\text{ km}$ apart from each other on a highway. A car starts from A and another car from B at the same time. If they move in the same direction, they meet each other in $6\text{ hours}$. If they move in the opposite direction towards each other, they meet in $1\text{ hour } 30\text{ minutes}$. Find the speeds of the cars (in km/h).
solution:
Same direction: $x - y = \frac{60}{6} = 10\text{ km/h}$.

Opposite direction ($1.5\text{ h}$): $x + y = \frac{60}{1.5} = 40\text{ km/h}$.

$x = \frac{40 + 10}{2} = 25\text{ km/h}$, and $y = \frac{40 - 10}{2} = 15\text{ km/h}$.

questionText: Places A and B are $20\text{ km}$ apart on the highway. A car starts from A and another from B at the same time. If the cars travel in the same direction at different speeds, they meet in one hour. If they travelled towards each other, they met in $12\text{ minutes}$. What are the speeds (in km/h) of two cars?
solution:
Same direction: $x - y = \frac{20}{1} = 20\text{ km/h}$.

Towards each other ($12\text{ min} = 0.2\text{ h}$): $x + y = \frac{20}{0.2} = 100\text{ km/h}$.

$x = \frac{100 + 20}{2} = 60\text{ km/h}$, and $y = \frac{100 - 20}{2} = 40\text{ km/h}$.

questionText: A train starts running at a uniform speed of $60\text{ km/h}$ from station P towards station Q. At the same time another train starts running from station Q towards station P. If the distance between the stations P and Q is $275\text{ km}$ and the trains meet in two and a half hours, then what is the speed of the train running towards station P in km/h?
solution:
$\text{Relative speed} = \frac{\text{Total distance}}{\text{Time to meet}} = \frac{275}{2.5} = 110\text{ km/h}$.

Since trains travel towards each other: $60 + v = 110 \implies v = 50\text{ km/h}$.

questionText: Two tourist buses start from the same point and move along two roads at right angles at speeds of $48\text{ km/h}$ and $36\text{ km/h}$, respectively. The distance between the buses after $15\text{ seconds}$ is
solution:
$48\text{ km/h} = 48 \times \frac{5}{18} = \frac{40}{3}\text{ m/s}$. In $15\text{ s}$, distance $= \frac{40}{3} \times 15 = 200\text{ m}$.

$36\text{ km/h} = 36 \times \frac{5}{18} = 10\text{ m/s}$. In $15\text{ s}$, distance $= 10 \times 15 = 150\text{ m}$.

Since the roads are at right angles: $\text{Distance} = \sqrt{200^2 + 150^2} = \sqrt{40000 + 22500} = \sqrt{62500} = 250\text{ m}$.

questionText: The distance between two places A and B is $140\text{ km}$. Two cars x and y start simultaneously from A and B, respectively. If they move in the same direction, they meet after $7\text{ hours}$. If they move towards each other, they meet after one hour. What is the speed (in km/h) of car y if its speed is more than that of car x?
solution:
Same direction: $y - x = \frac{140}{7} = 20\text{ km/h}$.

Towards each other: $y + x = \frac{140}{1} = 140\text{ km/h}$.

Adding equations: $2y = 160 \implies y = 80\text{ km/h}$.

questionText: Places A and B are $45\text{ km}$ apart from each other. A car starts from place A and another car starts from place B at the same time. If they move in the same direction, they meet in $4\frac{1}{2}\text{ h}$ and if they move towards each other, they meet in $27\text{ minutes}$. What is the speed (in km/h) of the car which moves faster?
solution:
Same direction: $x - y = \frac{45}{4.5} = 10\text{ km/h}$.

Towards each other: $x + y = \frac{45}{27/60} = \frac{45 \times 60}{27} = 100\text{ km/h}$.

Faster car speed $x = \frac{100 + 10}{2} = 55\text{ km/h}$.

questionText: The driver of a car, which is travelling at a speed of $75\text{ km/h}$, locates a bus $80\text{ m}$ ahead of him, travelling in the same direction. After $15\text{ seconds}$, he finds that the bus is $40\text{ m}$ behind the car. What is the speed of the bus (in km/h)?
solution:
Total relative distance gained by car $= 80 + 40 = 120\text{ m}$.

$\text{Relative speed} = \frac{120\text{ m}}{15\text{ s}} = 8\text{ m/s} = 8 \times \frac{18}{5} = 28.8\text{ km/h}$.

$\text{Speed of bus} = 75 - 28.8 = 46.2\text{ km/h}$.

questionText: On a straight road, a bus is $30\text{ km}$ ahead of a car travelling in the same direction. After $3\text{ hours}$, the car is $60\text{ km}$ ahead of the bus. If the speed of the bus is $42\text{ km/h}$, then find the speed of the car.
solution:
Net relative distance covered by car $= 30 + 60 = 90\text{ km}$.

$\text{Relative speed} = \frac{90}{3} = 30\text{ km/h}$.

$\text{Speed of car} = 42 + 30 = 72\text{ km/h}$.

questionText: A car and a bus were travelling in the same direction. At 7:30 a.m. the car travelling at a speed of $72\text{ km/h}$ was $4.2\text{ km}$ behind the bus. At 8:15 a.m. the car was $15.8\text{ km}$ ahead of the bus. What is the ratio of the speed of the car to the speed of the bus?
solution:
Time interval from 7:30 to 8:15 a.m. $= 45\text{ minutes} = \frac{3}{4}\text{ hour}$.

Relative distance gained $= 4.2 + 15.8 = 20\text{ km}$.

$\text{Relative speed} = \frac{20}{\frac{3}{4}} = \frac{80}{3}\text{ km/h}$.

$S_{\text{car}} - S_{\text{bus}} = \frac{80}{3} \implies S_{\text{bus}} = 72 - \frac{80}{3} = \frac{136}{3}\text{ km/h}$.

$\text{Ratio} = \frac{S_{\text{car}}}{S_{\text{bus}}} = \frac{72}{\frac{136}{3}} = \frac{216}{136} = \frac{27}{17}$.

questionText: Two trains start from Delhi and Puna towards each other at 7 am with speeds of $85\text{ km/h}$ and $67\text{ km/h}$, respectively. If they cross each other at 3.30 p.m., the distance between the stations is:
solution:
Time elapsed from 7:00 am to 3:30 pm $= 8.5\text{ hours}$.

$\text{Relative speed} = 85 + 67 = 152\text{ km/h}$.

$\text{Distance} = 152 \times 8.5 = 1292\text{ km}$.

questionText: The distance between two stations, A and B, is $575\text{ km}$. A train starts from station A at 3:00 p.m. and moves towards station 'B' at an average speed of $50\text{ km/h}$. Another train starts from station 'B' at 3:30 p.m. and moves towards station 'A' at an average speed of $60\text{ km/h}$. How far from station 'A' will the trains meet?
solution:
Distance covered by train A from 3:00 to 3:30 p.m. ($0.5\text{ h}$) $= 50 \times 0.5 = 25\text{ km}$.

Remaining distance at 3:30 p.m. $= 575 - 25 = 550\text{ km}$.

Relative speed $= 50 + 60 = 110\text{ km/h}$.

Time taken to meet after 3:30 p.m. $= \frac{550}{110} = 5\text{ hours}$.

$\text{Distance from station A} = 25 + (50 \times 5) = 25 + 250 = 275\text{ km}$.

questionText: Two people A and B are at a distance of $220\text{ km}$ from each other at 10:30 AM. After $30\text{ minutes}$, A starts moving towards B at the speed of $40\text{ km/hr}$ while at 12 P.M. B starts moving away from A at a speed of $30\text{ km/hr}$. At what time will they meet on the next day?
solution:
At 11:00 AM, A starts moving towards B at $40\text{ km/hr}$.
From 11:00 AM to 12:00 PM ($1\text{ hour}$), A covers $40 \times 1 = 40\text{ km}$.

At 12:00 PM, distance between them $= 220 - 40 = 180\text{ km}$.

Since B moves away at $30\text{ km/hr}$ and A pursues at $40\text{ km/hr}$, relative speed $= 40 - 30 = 10\text{ km/hr}$.

$\text{Time to meet} = \frac{180}{10} = 18\text{ hours}$.

$\text{Meeting time} = \text{12:00 PM} + 18\text{ hours} = \text{6:00 AM next day}$.

questionText: A and B leave from point M at the same time towards point N. B reaches N and starts towards M instantly. He meets A at point O (between M and N). The distance between M and N is $245\text{ km}$. If the speeds of A and B are $26\text{ km/h}$ and $65\text{ km/h}$, respectively, then what is the distance between O and N?
solution:
Total distance covered by A and B combined $= 2 \times MN = 2 \times 245 = 490\text{ km}$.

Ratio of speeds of A and B $= 26 : 65 = 2 : 5$.

Distance covered by A $= 490 \times \frac{2}{7} = 140\text{ km} = MO$.

$\text{Distance between O and N} = MN - MO = 245 - 140 = 105\text{ km}$.

questionText: Akshara and Siddharth travel from point P to Q, a distance of $72\text{ km}$ at a rate of $8\text{ km/h}$ and $10\text{ km/h}$, respectively. Siddharth reaches Q first and returns immediately and meets Akshara at R. Find the distance from P to R.
solution:
Total distance travelled by both $= 2 \times 72 = 144\text{ km}$.

Ratio of speeds of Akshara and Siddharth $= 8 : 10 = 4 : 5$.

$\text{Distance covered by Akshara (PR)} = 144 \times \frac{4}{9} = 64\text{ km}$.

questionText: Menu and Daya travel from point A to B, a distance of $105\text{ km}$, at speeds of $10\text{ km/h}$ and $25\text{ km/h}$, respectively. Daya reaches point B first and returns immediately and meets Menu at point C. Find the distance from point A to point C.
solution:
Total distance travelled by Menu and Daya combined $= 2 \times 105 = 210\text{ km}$.

Ratio of speeds of Menu and Daya $= 10 : 25 = 2 : 5$.

$\text{Distance covered by Menu (AC)} = 210 \times \frac{2}{7} = 60\text{ km}$.

questionText:
Two places B1 and B2 are $500\text{ km}$ apart from each other. Sonit and Robin start moving from B1 towards B2 at the same time. After reaching B2, they return back to B1. Speed of Sonit is $80\text{ km/hr}$ more than the Robin. If they meet after $6\text{ hours}$, then which of the following statements is /are correct?
I. Distance covered by Sonit is 600 km.
II. Speed of Robin is $\frac{120}{3}\text{ km/hr}$.
solution:
Total distance covered by both in $6\text{ hours} = 2 \times 500 = 1000\text{ km}$.

Sum of speeds $= \frac{1000}{6} = \frac{500}{3}\text{ km/hr}$.

Given $S_{\text{Sonit}} - S_{\text{Robin}} = 80 = \frac{240}{3}\text{ km/hr}$.

$S_{\text{Sonit}} = \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{500}{3} + \frac{240}{3}\right) = \frac{370}{3}\text{ km/hr}$.
Distance covered by Sonit in $6\text{ hours} = 6 \times \frac{370}{3} = 740\text{ km} \ne 600\text{ km}$ (Statement I is false).

$S_{\text{Robin}} = \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{500}{3} - \frac{240}{3}\right) = \frac{130}{3}\text{ km/hr} \ne \frac{120}{3}\text{ km/hr}$ (Statement II is false).

Hence, Neither I nor II is correct.

questionText: A and B are two stations $420\text{ km}$ apart. A train starts from A at 11 am and travels towards B at the speed of $70\text{ kmph}$. Another train starts from B at 12 noon and travels towards A at the speed of $30\text{ kmph}$. At what time do they meet?
solution:
Distance covered by train A from 11 am to 12 noon ($1\text{ hour}$) $= 70\text{ km}$.

Remaining distance at 12 noon $= 420 - 70 = 350\text{ km}$.

Relative speed $= 70 + 30 = 100\text{ km/h}$.

Time taken to meet $= \frac{350}{100} = 3.5\text{ hours} = 3\text{ hours } 30\text{ minutes}$.

$\text{Meeting time} = \text{12 noon} + 3.5\text{ hours} = \text{3:30 pm}$.

questionText: Vinay and Mahesh are $250\text{ metres}$ apart from each other. They are moving towards each other with the speed of $36\text{ km/hr}$ and $54\text{ km/hr}$ respectively. In how much time will they meet each other?
solution:
$\text{Relative speed} = 36 + 54 = 90\text{ km/hr} = 90 \times \frac{5}{18} = 25\text{ m/s}$.

$\text{Time taken to meet} = \frac{250}{25} = 10\text{ seconds}$.

questionText: A train leaves Hyderabad at 4:00 A.M. and reaches Vijayawada at 8:00 A.M. the same day. Another train leaves Vijayawada at 6:00 A.M. and reaches Hyderabad at 9:30 A.M the same day. At what time do the two trains cross each other?
solution:
Time taken by Train 1 (Hyderabad to Vijayawada) $= 4\text{ hours}$.

Time taken by Train 2 (Vijayawada to Hyderabad) $= 3.5\text{ hours} = \frac{7}{2}\text{ hours}$.

Let distance $= 28\text{ units}$.
Speed of Train 1 $= \frac{28}{4} = 7\text{ units/h}$.
Speed of Train 2 $= \frac{28}{3.5} = 8\text{ units/h}$.

Distance covered by Train 1 from 4:00 to 6:00 A.M. ($2\text{ hours}$) $= 7 \times 2 = 14\text{ units}$.
Remaining distance at 6:00 A.M. $= 28 - 14 = 14\text{ units}$.

Relative speed $= 7 + 8 = 15\text{ units/h}$.
Time after 6:00 A.M. $= \frac{14}{15}\text{ hours} = \frac{14}{15} \times 60 = 56\text{ minutes}$.

$\text{Crossing time} = \text{6:56 A.M.}$

questionText: Ram starts from point A at 8 a.m. and reaches point B at 2 p.m. on the same day. On the same day, Raju starts from point B at 8 a.m. and reaches point A at 6 p.m. on the same day. Both points A and B are separated by only a straight line track. At what time they both meet?
solution:
Time taken by Ram $t_1 = 6\text{ hours}$ (8 a.m. to 2 p.m.).

Time taken by Raju $t_2 = 10\text{ hours}$ (8 a.m. to 6 p.m.).

Since both start at the same time (8 a.m.):
$\text{Time to meet} = \frac{t_1 \times t_2}{t_1 + t_2} = \frac{6 \times 10}{6 + 10} = \frac{60}{16} = 3.75\text{ hours} = 3\text{ hours } 45\text{ minutes}$.

$\text{Meeting time} = \text{8:00 a.m.} + 3\text{ hours } 45\text{ minutes} = \text{11:45 a.m.}$

questionText: Two stations A and B are $230\text{ km}$ apart on a straight line. One train starts from A at 4 am and travels towards B at $40\text{ km/hr}$. Another train starts from B at 5 am and travels towards A at a speed of $55\text{ km/hr}$. At what time will they meet?
solution:
Distance covered by train A from 4 am to 5 am ($1\text{ hour}$) $= 40\text{ km}$.

Remaining distance at 5 am $= 230 - 40 = 190\text{ km}$.

Relative speed $= 40 + 55 = 95\text{ km/hr}$.

Time after 5 am $= \frac{190}{95} = 2\text{ hours}$.

$\text{Meeting time} = \text{5:00 a.m.} + 2\text{ hours} = \text{7:00 a.m.}$

questionText: Two stations are $120\text{ km}$ apart on a straight line. A train starts from station A at 8 a.m. and moves towards station B at $20\text{ km/h}$ and another train starts from station B at 9 a.m. and travels towards station A at a speed of $30\text{ km/h}$. At what time will they meet?
solution:
Distance covered by train A from 8 a.m. to 9 a.m. ($1\text{ hour}$) $= 20\text{ km}$.

Remaining distance at 9 a.m. $= 120 - 20 = 100\text{ km}$.

Relative speed $= 20 + 30 = 50\text{ km/h}$.

Time taken after 9 a.m. $= \frac{100}{50} = 2\text{ hours}$.

$\text{Meeting time} = \text{9:00 a.m.} + 2\text{ hours} = \text{11:00 a.m.}$

questionText: Two trains whose lengths are $450\text{ metres}$ and $300\text{ metres}$ are moving towards each other at the speed of $162\text{ km/hr}$ and $108\text{ km/hr}$ respectively. If distance between trains is $300\text{ metres}$, then in how much time, these trains will cross each other?
solution:
Total distance to be covered $= 450 + 300 + 300 = 1050\text{ metres}$.

$\text{Relative speed} = 162 + 108 = 270\text{ km/hr} = 270 \times \frac{5}{18} = 75\text{ m/s}$.

$\text{Time taken} = \frac{1050}{75} = 14\text{ seconds}$.

questionText: Two cities P and Q are $181\text{ km}$ apart on a straight road. One man starts from P at 8 : 30 A.M. and travels toward Q at $30\text{ km/h}$. If another man starts from Q at 8 : 54 A.M. and travels towards P at a speed of $35\text{ km/h}$, then at what time will they meet?
solution:
Time elapsed from 8:30 to 8:54 A.M. $= 24\text{ minutes} = \frac{24}{60} = 0.4\text{ hours}$.

Distance covered by first man $= 30 \times 0.4 = 12\text{ km}$.

Remaining distance at 8:54 A.M. $= 181 - 12 = 169\text{ km}$.

Relative speed $= 30 + 35 = 65\text{ km/h}$.

Time to meet $= \frac{169}{65} = 2.6\text{ hours} = 2\text{ hours } 36\text{ minutes}$.

$\text{Meeting time} = \text{8:54 A.M.} + 2\text{ hours } 36\text{ minutes} = \text{11:30 A.M.}$

questionText: Suppose A starts walking at a speed of $8\text{ km/h}$. After $8\text{ hours}$ B started travelling on a bicycle at a speed of $24\text{ km/h}$. The distance from the starting B can catch A is:
solution:
Head start of A in $8\text{ hours} = 8 \times 8 = 64\text{ km}$.

$\text{Relative speed} = 24 - 8 = 16\text{ km/h}$.

$\text{Time taken by B to catch A} = \frac{64}{16} = 4\text{ hours}$.

$\text{Distance from starting point} = 24 \times 4 = 96\text{ km}$.

questionText: Two stations $\text{T}_1$ and $\text{T}_2$ are $300\text{ km}$ apart. A car starts from station $\text{T}_1$ at 8 am and moves towards station $\text{T}_2$ at a speed of $45\text{ km/hr}$, and at 10 am another car starts from station $\text{T}_2$ towards $\text{T}_1$ at a speed of $60\text{ km/hr}$. Then the cars will meet at:
solution:
Distance covered by first car from 8 to 10 am ($2\text{ hours}$) $= 45 \times 2 = 90\text{ km}$.

Remaining distance at 10 am $= 300 - 90 = 210\text{ km}$.

Relative speed $= 45 + 60 = 105\text{ km/hr}$.

Time taken to meet $= \frac{210}{105} = 2\text{ hours}$.

$\text{Meeting time} = \text{10:00 am} + 2\text{ hours} = \text{12:00 pm}$.

questionText: Two towns P and Q are $275\text{ km}$ apart. A motorcycle rider starts from P towards Q at 10:00 a.m. at the speed of $25\text{ km/h}$. Another rider starts from Q towards P at 12 noon on the same day at the speed of $20\text{ km/h}$. At what time will they cross each other?
solution:
Distance covered by first rider from 10:00 a.m. to 12 noon ($2\text{ hours}$) $= 25 \times 2 = 50\text{ km}$.

Remaining distance at 12 noon $= 275 - 50 = 225\text{ km}$.

Relative speed $= 25 + 20 = 45\text{ km/h}$.

Time taken to meet $= \frac{225}{45} = 5\text{ hours}$.

$\text{Crossing time} = \text{12:00 noon} + 5\text{ hours} = \text{5:00 pm}$.

questionText: Two cities A and B are $135\text{ km}$ apart on a straight track. One car starts from A at 8 a.m. and travels towards B at $25\text{ km/h}$. Another car starts from B at 9 a.m. and travels towards A at a speed of $30\text{ km/h}$. At what time will they meet?
solution:
Distance covered by car from A in $1\text{ hour}$ (8 to 9 a.m.) $= 25\text{ km}$.

Remaining distance at 9 a.m. $= 135 - 25 = 110\text{ km}$.

Relative speed $= 25 + 30 = 55\text{ km/h}$.

Time taken to meet after 9 a.m. $= \frac{110}{55} = 2\text{ hours}$.

$\text{Meeting time} = \text{9:00 a.m.} + 2\text{ hours} = \text{11:00 a.m.}$

questionText: Ajit Singh left from place P at 9.30 a.m. for place Q, and David Raj left place Q at 1.30 p.m. for place P. The distance between them is $416\text{ km}$. If Ajit Singh's speed is $44\text{ km/h}$ and David Raj's speed is $52\text{ km/h}$, then at what time will they meet each other?
solution:
Ajit Singh travels alone from 9:30 a.m. to 1:30 p.m. ($4\text{ hours}$): $44 \times 4 = 176\text{ km}$.

Remaining distance at 1:30 p.m. $= 416 - 176 = 240\text{ km}$.

Relative speed $= 44 + 52 = 96\text{ km/h}$.

Time taken after 1:30 p.m. $= \frac{240}{96} = 2.5\text{ hours} = 2\text{ hours } 30\text{ minutes}$.

$\text{Meeting time} = \text{1:30 p.m.} + 2\text{ hours } 30\text{ minutes} = \text{4:00 p.m.}$

questionText: Veena and Karmesh were at different places in Delhi. They fixed a meeting point to meet to settle some issue. Veena started her journey at 8:00 a.m. from place A and reached place B at 4:00 p.m. and Karmesh started moving from place B $2\text{ hours}$ later than the time Veena started and could reach place A at 5:00 p.m. the same day, via the same route. At what time will Karmesh and Veena meet each other?
solution:
Time taken by Veena (8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.) $= 8\text{ hours}$.

Karmesh starts at 10:00 a.m. and reaches A at 5:00 p.m., time taken $= 7\text{ hours}$.

Let total distance $= \text{LCM}(8, 7) = 56\text{ km}$.
Speed of Veena $= \frac{56}{8} = 7\text{ km/h}$, Speed of Karmesh $= \frac{56}{7} = 8\text{ km/h}$.

Distance covered by Veena from 8:00 to 10:00 a.m. ($2\text{ hours}$) $= 7 \times 2 = 14\text{ km}$.
Remaining distance at 10:00 a.m. $= 56 - 14 = 42\text{ km}$.

Relative speed $= 7 + 8 = 15\text{ km/h}$.
Time after 10:00 a.m. $= \frac{42}{15} = 2.8\text{ hours} = 2\text{ hours } 48\text{ minutes}$.

$\text{Meeting time} = \text{10:00 a.m.} + 2\text{ hours } 48\text{ minutes} = \text{12:48 p.m.}$

questionText: A runner starts running from a point at 5:00 am at the speed of $10\text{ km/hr}$. Second runner starts from the same point at 8:00 am in the same direction with a speed of $15\text{ km/hr}$. At what time of the day will the second runner will overtake the first runner?
solution:
Distance covered by first runner from 5:00 to 8:00 am ($3\text{ hours}$) $= 10 \times 3 = 30\text{ km}$.

$\text{Relative speed} = 15 - 10 = 5\text{ km/hr}$.

$\text{Time taken to overtake} = \frac{30}{5} = 6\text{ hours}$.

$\text{Overtaking time} = \text{8:00 am} + 6\text{ hours} = \text{2:00 pm}$.

questionText: A train leaves station A at 8 am and reaches station B at 12 noon. A car leaves station B at 8:30 am and reaches station A at the same time when the train reaches station B. At what time do they meet?
solution:
Time taken by train (8:00 am to 12:00 noon) $= 4\text{ hours}$.

Time taken by car (8:30 am to 12:00 noon) $= 3.5\text{ hours} = \frac{7}{2}\text{ hours}$.

Let distance $= 28\text{ km}$. Train speed $= \frac{28}{4} = 7\text{ km/h}$, Car speed $= \frac{28}{3.5} = 8\text{ km/h}$.

Distance covered by train in first $30\text{ minutes} = 7 \times 0.5 = 3.5\text{ km}$.
Remaining distance at 8:30 am $= 28 - 3.5 = 24.5\text{ km}$.

Relative speed $= 7 + 8 = 15\text{ km/h}$.
Time after 8:30 am $= \frac{24.5}{15} = \frac{49}{30}\text{ hours} = 1\text{ hour } 38\text{ minutes}$.

$\text{Meeting time} = \text{8:30 am} + 1\text{ hr } 38\text{ min} = \text{10:08 am}$.

questionText: Two trains start at the same time from stations P and Q and travel towards each other at the speeds of $75\text{ km/h}$ and $100\text{ km/h}$, respectively. When they meet, it is found that one train has travelled $50\text{ km}$ more than the other. The distance (in km) between two stations is:
solution:
Since time is constant until meeting, $\frac{D_1}{D_2} = \frac{S_1}{S_2} = \frac{100}{75} = \frac{4}{3}$.

Difference in distance $= 4 - 3 = 1\text{ unit} = 50\text{ km}$.

$\text{Total distance} = (4 + 3) \times 50 = 7 \times 50 = 350\text{ km}$.

questionText: Julie and Soma start from the same point and walk in opposite directions. Julie walks $4\text{ km/h}$ faster than Soma. After $4\text{ hours}$ they are $40\text{ km}$ apart. How fast did each walk?
solution:
Opposite directions: $\text{Relative speed} = \frac{40\text{ km}}{4\text{ hours}} = 10\text{ km/h}$.

$v_{\text{Julie}} + v_{\text{Soma}} = 10\text{ km/h}$, and $v_{\text{Julie}} - v_{\text{Soma}} = 4\text{ km/h}$.

$v_{\text{Julie}} = \frac{10 + 4}{2} = 7\text{ km/h}$, and $v_{\text{Soma}} = \frac{10 - 4}{2} = 3\text{ km/h}$.

questionText: A dog takes $5\text{ leaps}$ for every $6\text{ leaps}$ of a hare, but $4\text{ leaps}$ of the dog are equal to $5\text{ leaps}$ of the hare. The ratio of the speed of dog and hare is?
solution:
Given $4\text{ leaps of dog} = 5\text{ leaps of hare} \implies 1\text{ leap of dog} = \frac{5}{4}\text{ leaps of hare}$.

$\text{Speed ratio} = \frac{5 \times \text{leap of dog}}{6 \times \text{leap of hare}} = \frac{5 \times \frac{5}{4}}{6 \times 1} = \frac{25}{24}$.

questionText: A is chasing B in the same interval of time. A jumps $8\text{ times}$, while B jumps $6\text{ times}$. But the distance covered by A in $7\text{ jumps}$ is the same as that of B in $5\text{ jumps}$. The ratio between the speeds of A and B is
solution:
Given $7 d_A = 5 d_B \implies d_A = \frac{5}{7} d_B$.

$\frac{\text{Speed of A}}{\text{Speed of B}} = \frac{8 \times d_A}{6 \times d_B} = \frac{8 \times \frac{5}{7}}{6} = \frac{40}{42} = \frac{20}{21}$.

questionText: A bus start from a bus stand after every $50\text{ minutes}$ in the same direction. Mohit is walking in opposite direction with a speed of $50\text{ km/hr}$. If Mohit meets each bus in $10\text{ minutes}$, then what is the speed of bus?
solution:
Distance between consecutive buses $= v_{\text{bus}} \times 50\text{ min}$.

Relative speed $= v_{\text{bus}} + 50\text{ km/hr}$.

$(v_{\text{bus}} + 50) \times 10 = v_{\text{bus}} \times 50 \implies 10 v_{\text{bus}} + 500 = 50 v_{\text{bus}} \implies 40 v_{\text{bus}} = 500 \implies v_{\text{bus}} = 12.5\text{ km/hr}$.

questionText: Two guns are fired at $13\text{ minutes}$ interval. But the passenger in the train hears the sound of second gun after $12\text{ minute } 30\text{ seconds}$ of the first. If the speed of sound is $330\text{ m/s}$ then the speed of train was.
solution:
Difference in time for sound $= 13\text{ min} - 12\text{ min } 30\text{ sec} = 30\text{ seconds}$.

Distance covered by sound in $30\text{ s}$ equals distance covered by train in $12.5\text{ minutes} = 750\text{ seconds}$.

$v_{\text{train}} \times 750 = 330 \times 30 \implies v_{\text{train}} = \frac{9900}{750} = 13.2\text{ m/s}$.

In km/hr: $13.2 \times \frac{18}{5} = 47.52\text{ km/hr} = 47\frac{52}{100} = 47\frac{13}{25}\text{ km/hr}$.

questionText: Travelling a distance of $1000\text{ km}$, a train slowed down due to repairs of the tracks. Its average speed for the trip reduced by $75\text{ km/h}$ and the time of travel increased by $3\text{ hours}$. The original duration of the travel is:
solution:
Let original time be $T\text{ hours}$. Original speed $= \frac{1000}{T}$, reduced speed $= \frac{1000}{T+3}$.

$\frac{1000}{T} - \frac{1000}{T+3} = 75 \implies \frac{1}{T} - \frac{1}{T+3} = \frac{3}{40} \implies \frac{3}{T(T+3)} = \frac{3}{40} \implies T(T+3) = 40$.

$T^2 + 3T - 40 = 0 \implies (T - 5)(T + 8) = 0 \implies T = 5\text{ hours}$.

questionText: The distance between two places is $1200\text{ km}$. To cover this distance, a person X takes $5\text{ hours}$ lesser than another person Y, whose average speed is $40\text{ km/h}$ lesser than that of X. The time taken by Y to complete the travel is:
solution:
Let time taken by Y be $T_Y$. Then time taken by X is $T_Y - 5$.

$\frac{1200}{T_Y - 5} - \frac{1200}{T_Y} = 40 \implies \frac{30}{T_Y - 5} - \frac{30}{T_Y} = 1 \implies \frac{150}{T_Y(T_Y - 5)} = 1 \implies T_Y^2 - 5T_Y - 150 = 0$.

$(T_Y - 15)(T_Y + 10) = 0 \implies T_Y = 15\text{ hours}$.

questionText: A fast local of Mumbai takes $45\text{ minutes}$ less than a slow local for a journey of $150\text{ km}$. If the speed of the fast local is $10\text{ km/h}$ more than that of the slow local, find the speed (in km/h) of the slow local train.
solution:
Let the speed of the slow local be $v\text{ km/h}$. Fast local speed $= v + 10\text{ km/h}$.

$\frac{150}{v} - \frac{150}{v+10} = \frac{45}{60} = \frac{3}{4} \implies \frac{50 \times 10}{v(v+10)} = \frac{1}{4} \implies v(v+10) = 2000$.

$v^2 + 10v - 2000 = 0 \implies (v - 40)(v + 50) = 0 \implies v = 40\text{ km/h}$.

questionText: A car left $60\text{ minutes}$ early than the scheduled time but in order to reach its destination $280\text{ km}$ away in time, it has to slow its usual speed by $14\text{ km/hr}$. What is the usual speed of the car?
solution:
Let usual speed be $v\text{ km/hr}$. Increased time $= 60\text{ minutes} = 1\text{ hour}$.

$\frac{280}{v - 14} - \frac{280}{v} = 1 \implies \frac{280 \times 14}{v(v - 14)} = 1 \implies v(v - 14) = 3920$.

Since $70 \times 56 = 3920$, we have $v = 70\text{ km/hr}$.

questionText: A journey of $180\text{ km}$ takes $6\text{ hours}$ more when the speed of a bike is reduced by $8\text{ km/h}$. What is the original speed of the bike?
solution:
Let original speed be $v\text{ km/h}$.

$\frac{180}{v - 8} - \frac{180}{v} = 6 \implies \frac{30}{v - 8} - \frac{30}{v} = 1 \implies \frac{240}{v(v - 8)} = 1 \implies v(v - 8) = 240$.

Since $20 \times 12 = 240$, we have $v = 20\text{ km/h}$.

questionText: A person travels a distance of $300\text{ km}$ and then returns to the starting point. The time taken by him for the outward journey is $5\text{ hours}$ more than the time taken for the return journey. If he returns at a speed of $10\text{ km/h}$ more than the speed of going, what is the average speed (in km/h) for the entire journey?
solution:
Let outward speed be $v\text{ km/h}$. Return speed $= v + 10\text{ km/h}$.

$\frac{300}{v} - \frac{300}{v+10} = 5 \implies \frac{60}{v} - \frac{60}{v+10} = 1 \implies \frac{600}{v(v+10)} = 1 \implies v(v+10) = 600$.

$v = 20\text{ km/h}$. Return speed $= 30\text{ km/h}$.

$\text{Average speed} = \frac{2 \times 20 \times 30}{20 + 30} = \frac{1200}{50} = 24\text{ km/h}$.

questionText: The speed of train A is $25\text{ km/hr}$ more than the speed of train B. A takes $4\text{ hours}$ less time to travel a distance of $300\text{ km}$ what train B takes to travel $250\text{ km}$. What is the speed (in km/ hr) of A?
solution:
Let the speed of train A be $v_A\text{ km/hr}$. Then speed of train B $= v_A - 25\text{ km/hr}$.

$\frac{250}{v_A - 25} - \frac{300}{v_A} = 4$.

Substituting $v_A = 50\text{ km/hr}$:
$\frac{250}{25} - \frac{300}{50} = 10 - 6 = 4\text{ hours}$.

Thus, speed of train A is $50\text{ km/hr}$.

questionText: A covered a distance of $240\text{ km}$ at a certain speed. Had his speed been $8\text{ km/h}$ less, then the time taken would have been one hour more for covering the same distance. How much time (in hours) will he take to cover a distance of $480\text{ km}$ at his original speed?
solution:
Let original speed be $v\text{ km/h}$.

$\frac{240}{v - 8} - \frac{240}{v} = 1 \implies \frac{1920}{v(v - 8)} = 1 \implies v(v - 8) = 1920$.

Since $48 \times 40 = 1920$, we have $v = 48\text{ km/h}$.

$\text{Time to cover } 480\text{ km at original speed} = \frac{480}{48} = 10\text{ hours}$.

questionText: A part of the journey is covered in $22.5\text{ minutes}$ at a speed of $68\text{ km/h}$ and the remaining part in $12\text{ minutes}$ at a speed of $72\text{ km/h}$. The total distance of the journey is (to the nearest integer):
solution:
$D_1 = 68 \times \frac{22.5}{60} = 68 \times \frac{3}{8} = 25.5\text{ km}$.

$D_2 = 72 \times \frac{12}{60} = 72 \times 0.2 = 14.4\text{ km}$.

$\text{Total distance} = 25.5 + 14.4 = 39.9\text{ km} \approx 40\text{ km}$.

questionText: A car starts running at an initial speed of $60\text{km/h}$, with its speed increasing every hour by $10\text{km/h}$. How many hours will it take to cover a distance of $1210\text{km}$?
solution:
Distance in each hour forms an arithmetic progression: $a = 60$, $d = 10$.

$S_n = \frac{n}{2}[2(60) + (n-1)10] = \frac{n}{2}[110 + 10n] = 5n^2 + 55n$.

$5n^2 + 55n = 1210 \implies n^2 + 11n - 242 = 0 \implies (n - 11)(n + 22) = 0 \implies n = 11\text{ hours}$.

questionText: A delivery boy started from his office at 10 a.m. to deliver an article. He ride his scooter at a speed of $32\text{ km/h}$. He delivered the article and waited for $15\text{ minutes}$ to get the payment. After the payment was made, he reached his office at 11.25 a.m., travelling at a speed of $24\text{ km/h}$. Find the total distance travelled by the boy.
solution:
Total time elapsed from 10:00 to 11:25 a.m. $= 85\text{ minutes}$.

Travelling time $= 85 - 15 = 70\text{ minutes} = \frac{7}{6}\text{ hours}$.

Let one-way distance be $d\text{ km}$.
$\frac{d}{32} + \frac{d}{24} = \frac{7}{6} \implies d\left(\frac{3+4}{96}\right) = \frac{7}{6} \implies \frac{7d}{96} = \frac{7}{6} \implies d = 16\text{ km}$.

$\text{Total distance travelled} = 2d = 2 \times 16 = 32\text{ km}$.

questionText: Rashi travelled a distance of $400\text{ km}$ at an average speed of $50\text{ km/h}$. She covers the first half distance in the first lag in $2\text{ hours}$, while she covers another lag at half the speed of that of the first lag in $1\text{ hour}$. What is the speed (in km/h) of the remaining distance?
solution:
Total time $= \frac{400}{50} = 8\text{ hours}$.

First lag: distance $= \frac{400}{2} = 200\text{ km}$ in $2\text{ hours} \implies \text{Speed}_1 = \frac{200}{2} = 100\text{ km/h}$.

Second lag: speed $= \frac{100}{2} = 50\text{ km/h}$ for $1\text{ hour} \implies \text{Distance}_2 = 50 \times 1 = 50\text{ km}$.

Remaining distance $= 400 - 200 - 50 = 150\text{ km}$.
Remaining time $= 8 - 2 - 1 = 5\text{ hours}$.

$\text{Speed for remaining distance} = \frac{150}{5} = 30\text{ km/h}$.

questionText: Smita is faster than Pihu. Smita and Pihu each walk $48\text{ km}$. The sum of their speeds is $14\text{ km/hr}$, and the sum of times taken by them is $28\text{ hours}$. What is Smita's speed?
solution:
Let speeds be $s$ and $p$ ($s > p$) with $s + p = 14$.

$\frac{48}{s} + \frac{48}{p} = 28 \implies 48\left(\frac{s+p}{sp}\right) = 28 \implies \frac{48 \times 14}{sp} = 28 \implies sp = 24$.

Since $s + p = 14$ and $sp = 24$, the roots are $12$ and $2$.

Since Smita is faster, Smita's speed is $12\text{ km/hr}$.

questionText: Ram needs to reach the examination centre in $6\text{ hours}$, the journey itself is $250\text{ km}$. If Ram has covered $\frac{3}{5}\text{th}$ of the distance in $3.5\text{ hours}$ then what is the speed required to reach the destination $30\text{ minutes}$ early than the required time?
solution:
Distance covered $= \frac{3}{5} \times 250 = 150\text{ km}$. Remaining distance $= 250 - 150 = 100\text{ km}$.

Total target time $= 6\text{ hours} - 0.5\text{ hours} = 5.5\text{ hours}$.

Time remaining $= 5.5 - 3.5 = 2\text{ hours}$.

$\text{Required speed} = \frac{100}{2} = 50\text{ km/hr}$.

questionText: Diameter of wheel of a cycle is $7\text{ cm}$. A cyclist takes $75\text{ minutes}$ to reach a destination at the speed of $36.3\text{ km/hr}$. How many revolutions will the wheel make during the journey?
solution:
$\text{Total distance} = 36.3 \times \frac{75}{60} = 45.375\text{ km} = 4537500\text{ cm}$.

Circumference of wheel $= \pi d = \frac{22}{7} \times 7 = 22\text{ cm}$.

$\text{Number of revolutions} = \frac{4537500}{22} = 206250$.

questionText: A car starts from point A towards point B, travelling at the speed of $20\text{ km/h}$. $1\frac{1}{2}\text{ hours}$ later, another car starts from point A and travelling at the speed of $30\text{ km/h}$ and reaches $2\frac{1}{2}\text{ hours}$ before the first car. Find the distance between A and B.
solution:
Difference in travel time between the two cars $= 1.5 + 2.5 = 4\text{ hours}$.

$\frac{D}{20} - \frac{D}{30} = 4 \implies \frac{3D - 2D}{60} = 4 \implies \frac{D}{60} = 4 \implies D = 240\text{ km}$.

questionText: R jogs at twice the speed of walking and runs at twice the speed of jogging. From his home to office, he covers half of the distance by walking and the rest by jogging. From his office to home, he covers half the distance jogging and the rest by running. What is his average speed (in km/h) in a complete round from his home to office and back home if the distance between his office and home is $10\text{ km}$ and he walks at the speed of $5\text{ km/h}$?
solution:
Speeds: Walking $= 5\text{ km/h}$, Jogging $= 10\text{ km/h}$, Running $= 20\text{ km/h}$.

Home to office ($10\text{ km}$):
- $5\text{ km}$ walking: $t_1 = \frac{5}{5} = 1\text{ hr}$.
- $5\text{ km}$ jogging: $t_2 = \frac{5}{10} = 0.5\text{ hr}$.

Office to home ($10\text{ km}$):
- $5\text{ km}$ jogging: $t_3 = \frac{5}{10} = 0.5\text{ hr}$.
- $5\text{ km}$ running: $t_4 = \frac{5}{20} = 0.25\text{ hr}$.

Total distance $= 20\text{ km}$, Total time $= 1 + 0.5 + 0.5 + 0.25 = 2.25 = \frac{9}{4}\text{ hours}$.

$\text{Average speed} = \frac{20}{\frac{9}{4}} = \frac{80}{9}\text{ km/h}$.

questionText: A person travels $5x$ distance at a speed of $5\text{ km/h}$, $x$ distance at a speed of $5\text{ km/h}$, and $4x$ distance at a speed of $6\text{ km/h}$ and takes a total of $112\text{ minutes}$. What is the total distance (in km) travelled by the person?
solution:
Total distance $= 5x + x + 4x = 10x$.

Total time $= \frac{5x}{5} + \frac{x}{5} + \frac{4x}{6} = x + 0.2x + \frac{2x}{3} = \frac{28x}{15}\text{ hours}$.

Given time $= 112\text{ minutes} = \frac{112}{60} = \frac{28}{15}\text{ hours}$.

$\frac{28x}{15} = \frac{28}{15} \implies x = 1$.

$\text{Total distance} = 10x = 10\text{ km}$.

questionText: Ram travelled from a place Z to P at an average speed of $130\text{ km/h}$. He travelled the first $75\%$ of the distance in two third of the time and the rest at an average speed of $x\text{ km/h}$. The value of $\frac{x}{2}$ is:
solution:
Let total distance be $D$ and total time be $T$, so $\frac{D}{T} = 130\text{ km/h}$.

Remaining distance $= 25\% D = \frac{D}{4}$.
Remaining time $= 1 - \frac{2}{3} = \frac{T}{3}$.

$x = \frac{D/4}{T/3} = \frac{3}{4} \frac{D}{T} = \frac{3}{4} \times 130 = 97.5\text{ km/h}$.

$\frac{x}{2} = \frac{97.5}{2} = 48.75$.

questionText: When a person travels at a speed of $8\frac{1}{3}\text{ m/sec}$, he will reach his destination on time. He covers $\frac{2}{3}$ of the journey in $\frac{5}{8}$ of the time. At what speed (in km/h) should he travel to cover the remaining distance to reach the destination on time?
solution:
Initial speed $= 8\frac{1}{3}\text{ m/s} = \frac{25}{3} \times \frac{18}{5} = 30\text{ km/h}$.

Remaining distance $= 1 - \frac{2}{3} = \frac{1}{3}\text{ of journey}$.

Remaining time $= 1 - \frac{5}{8} = \frac{3}{8}\text{ of time}$.

$\text{Required speed} = \frac{1/3}{3/8} \times 30 = \frac{8}{9} \times 30 = \frac{80}{3} = 26\frac{2}{3}\text{ km/h}$.

questionText: A train has to cover $370\text{ km}$ at a uniform speed. After running $100\text{ km}$, the train started runing at a speed $5\text{ km/h}$ less than its normal speed due to some technical fault. The train got delayed by $36\text{ minutes}$. What is the normal speed of the train, in km/h?
solution:
Remaining distance $= 370 - 100 = 270\text{ km}$.

$\frac{270}{v - 5} - \frac{270}{v} = \frac{36}{60} = \frac{3}{5} \implies \frac{90 \times 5}{v(v - 5)} = \frac{1}{5} \implies v(v - 5) = 2250$.

Since $50 \times 45 = 2250$, the normal speed of the train is $50\text{ km/h}$.

questionText: A train runs first $75\text{ km}$ at a certain uniform speed and next $90\text{ km}$ at an average speed of $10\text{ km/h}$ more than the normal speed. If it takes $3\text{ hours}$ to complete the journey, then how much time will the train take to cover $300\text{ km}$ with normal speed?
solution:
$\frac{75}{v} + \frac{90}{v+10} = 3 \implies \frac{25}{v} + \frac{30}{v+10} = 1$.

Testing $v = 50\text{ km/h}$:
$\frac{25}{50} + \frac{30}{60} = 0.5 + 0.5 = 1$.
Normal speed $v = 50\text{ km/h}$.

$\text{Time to cover } 300\text{ km} = \frac{300}{50} = 6\text{ hours}$.

questionText: Akhil takes $30\text{ minutes}$ extra to cover a distance of $150\text{ km}$ if he drives $10\text{ km/h}$ slower than his usual speed. How much time will he take to drive $90\text{ km}$ if he drives $15\text{ km/h}$ slower than his usual speed?
solution:
$\frac{150}{v - 10} - \frac{150}{v} = \frac{30}{60} = 0.5 \implies \frac{1500}{v(v - 10)} = 0.5 \implies v(v - 10) = 3000$.

Since $60 \times 50 = 3000$, usual speed $v = 60\text{ km/h}$.

Reduced speed $= 60 - 15 = 45\text{ km/h}$.

$\text{Time to drive } 90\text{ km} = \frac{90}{45} = 2\text{ hours}$.

questionText: A takes $2\text{ hours}$ more than B to cover a distance of $40\text{ km}$. If A doubles his speed, he takes $1\frac{1}{2}\text{ hour}$ more than B to cover $80\text{ km}$. To cover a distance of $120\text{ km}$, how much time (in hours) will B take travelling at his same speed?
solution:
Let speeds of A and B be $v_A$ and $v_B$.

$\frac{40}{v_A} - \frac{40}{v_B} = 2 \implies \frac{40}{v_A} = 2 + \frac{40}{v_B}$.

With double speed for $80\text{ km}$:
$\frac{80}{2v_A} - \frac{80}{v_B} = 1.5 \implies \frac{40}{v_A} - \frac{80}{v_B} = 1.5$.

Substituting: $2 + \frac{40}{v_B} - \frac{80}{v_B} = 1.5 \implies \frac{40}{v_B} = 0.5 \implies v_B = 80\text{ km/h}$.

$\text{Time for B to cover } 120\text{ km} = \frac{120}{80} = 1.5\text{ hours} = 1\frac{1}{2}\text{ hours}$.

questionText: Mohan takes $2\text{ hours}$ more than Kishore to walk $63\text{ km}$. If Mohan increases his speed by $50\%$, then he can make it in $1\text{ hour}$ less than Kishore. How much time does Kishore take to walk $63\text{ km}$?
solution:
Let Kishore's time be $T_K$. Mohan's initial time $T_M = T_K + 2$.

When Mohan's speed increases by $50\%$ (speed becomes $\frac{3}{2}$), his time becomes $\frac{2}{3} T_M$.

Given $\frac{2}{3} T_M = T_K - 1$.

Substituting $T_K = T_M - 2$:
$\frac{2}{3} T_M = T_M - 2 - 1 = T_M - 3 \implies \frac{1}{3} T_M = 3 \implies T_M = 9\text{ hours}$.

$\text{Kishore's time} T_K = 9 - 2 = 7\text{ hours}$.

questionText: The speed of a car is $40\%$ more than that of a bus. A train covers $1020\text{ km}$ in $8\frac{1}{2}\text{ hours}$. How much distance will the car cover in $1\frac{3}{4}\text{ hours}$ if the speed of the bus is half the speed of the train?
solution:
Speed of train $= \frac{1020}{8.5} = 120\text{ km/h}$.

Speed of bus $= \frac{120}{2} = 60\text{ km/h}$.

Speed of car $= 1.4 \times 60 = 84\text{ km/h}$.

$\text{Distance covered by car in } 1\frac{3}{4}\text{ hours} (\frac{7}{4}\text{ h}) = 84 \times \frac{7}{4} = 21 \times 7 = 147\text{ km}$.

questionText: A person moved from place A for place B at 2 p.m. at a speed of $4.5\text{ km/h}$, stayed at place B for $1.5\text{ hours}$ and returned to place A at a speed of $6\text{ km/h}$. He came back to place A at 7 p.m. What is the distance between places A and B (in km)?
solution:
Total time from 2 p.m. to 7 p.m. $= 5\text{ hours}$.

Travel time $= 5 - 1.5 = 3.5\text{ hours} = \frac{7}{2}\text{ hours}$.

Let distance between A and B be $d\text{ km}$.
$\frac{d}{4.5} + \frac{d}{6} = \frac{7}{2} \implies \frac{2d}{9} + \frac{d}{6} = \frac{7}{2} \implies \frac{7d}{18} = \frac{7}{2} \implies d = 9\text{ km}$.

questionText: A takes $2\text{ hours } 30\text{ minutes}$ more than B to walk $40\text{ km}$. If A doubles his speed, then he can make it in $1\text{ hour}$ less than B. How much time (in hours) does A require for walking a $40\text{ km}$ distance?
solution:
Let initial time taken by A be $T_A$.

Doubling speed halves the time: new time $= \frac{T_A}{2}$.

Time difference $= T_A - \frac{T_A}{2} = 2.5 - (-1) = 3.5\text{ hours}$.

$\frac{T_A}{2} = 3.5 \implies T_A = 7\text{ hours}$.

questionText: A takes $2\text{ hours}$ more than B to cover a distance of $40\text{ km}$. If A doubles his speed, he takes $1\frac{1}{2}\text{ hours}$ more than B to cover $80\text{ km}$. To cover a distance of $90\text{ km}$, how much time will B take travelling at his same speed?
solution:
$\frac{40}{v_A} - \frac{40}{v_B} = 2 \implies \frac{40}{v_A} = 2 + \frac{40}{v_B}$.

For $80\text{ km}$ at double speed:
$\frac{80}{2v_A} - \frac{80}{v_B} = 1.5 \implies \frac{40}{v_A} - \frac{80}{v_B} = 1.5$.

Substituting: $2 - \frac{40}{v_B} = 1.5 \implies \frac{40}{v_B} = 0.5 \implies v_B = 80\text{ km/h}$.

$\text{Time taken by B to cover } 90\text{ km} = \frac{90}{80} = \frac{9}{8} = 1\frac{1}{8}\text{ hours}$.

questionText: A person has to cover a distance of $160\text{ km}$ in $15\text{ hours}$. If he covers $\frac{4}{5}$ of the distance in $\frac{2}{3}$ of the time, then what should be his speed (in km/h) to cover the remaining distance in the remaining time?
solution:
Remaining distance $= 1 - \frac{4}{5} = \frac{1}{5} \times 160 = 32\text{ km}$.

Remaining time $= 1 - \frac{2}{3} = \frac{1}{3} \times 15 = 5\text{ hours}$.

$\text{Required speed} = \frac{32}{5} = 6.4\text{ km/h}$.

questionText: Travelling at $60\text{ km/h}$, a person reaches his destination in a certain time. He covers $60\%$ of his journey in $\frac{2}{5}\text{th}$ of the time. At what speed (in km/h) should he travel to cover the remaining journey so that he reaches the destination right on time?
solution:
Remaining distance $= 100\% - 60\% = 40\% = \frac{2}{5} D$.

Remaining time $= 1 - \frac{2}{5} = \frac{3}{5} T$.

$\text{Required speed} = \frac{\frac{2}{5} D}{\frac{3}{5} T} = \frac{2}{3} \times \frac{D}{T} = \frac{2}{3} \times 60 = 40\text{ km/h}$.

questionText: Speed of a train is $30\text{ percent}$ more than the speed of a car. Both start from point P at the same time and reach point Q at the same time. P and Q are $130\text{ km}$ apart from each other. On the way train stops for $30\text{ minutes}$ at a station. What is the speed of the train?
solution:
Ratio of speeds $\frac{S_{\text{train}}}{S_{\text{car}}} = \frac{130}{100} = \frac{13}{10}$.

Ratio of running times $= 10 : 13$.

Time difference $= 13 - 10 = 3\text{ units} = 30\text{ minutes} \implies 1\text{ unit} = 10\text{ minutes}$.

Running time of train $= 10 \times 10 = 100\text{ minutes} = \frac{5}{3}\text{ hours}$.

$\text{Speed of train} = \frac{130}{\frac{5}{3}} = 130 \times \frac{3}{5} = 78\text{ km/hr}$.

questionText: X and Y travel a distance of $90\text{ km}$ each such that the speed of Y is greater than that of X. The sum of their speeds is $100\text{ km/h}$ and the total time taken by both is $3\text{ hours } 45\text{ minutes}$. The ratio of the speed of X to that of Y is:
solution:
Total time $= 3\text{ h } 45\text{ m} = 3.75\text{ hours} = \frac{15}{4}\text{ hours}$.

$\frac{90}{x} + \frac{90}{y} = \frac{15}{4} \implies 90\left(\frac{x+y}{xy}\right) = \frac{15}{4}$.

Given $x + y = 100$:
$\frac{9000}{xy} = \frac{15}{4} \implies xy = \frac{9000 \times 4}{15} = 2400$.

With $x + y = 100$ and $xy = 2400$ (and $y > x$), $x = 40\text{ km/h}$ and $y = 60\text{ km/h}$.

$\text{Ratio } x : y = 40 : 60 = 2 : 3$.

questionText: Two cyclist X and Y start at the same time from place A and go towards place B at a speed of $6\text{ km/h}$ and $8\text{ km/h}$, respectively. Despite stopping for $15\text{ minutes}$ during the journey, Y reaches $10\text{ minutes}$ earlier than X. The distance between the places A and B is:
solution:
Net difference in cycling time $= 15 + 10 = 25\text{ minutes} = \frac{25}{60} = \frac{5}{12}\text{ hours}$.

$\frac{D}{6} - \frac{D}{8} = \frac{5}{12} \implies \frac{4D - 3D}{24} = \frac{5}{12} \implies \frac{D}{24} = \frac{5}{12} \implies D = 10\text{ km}$.

questionText: A man takes $6\text{ hours}$ to go to a place and come back by walking both the ways. He could have saved $2\text{ hours}$ by riding both the ways. The distance covered in the whole journey is $20\text{ miles}$. What is the average speed for the whole journey if he goes by walking and comes back by riding?
solution:
Time for walking both ways $= 6\text{ hours} \implies \text{Walking one way} = 3\text{ hours}$.

Time for riding both ways $= 6 - 2 = 4\text{ hours} \implies \text{Riding one way} = 2\text{ hours}$.

Time taken to walk one way and ride back $= 3 + 2 = 5\text{ hours}$.

$\text{Average speed} = \frac{\text{Total distance}}{\text{Total time}} = \frac{20}{5} = 4\text{ miles/hr}$.
